STRAIGHT-DOWN bird’s-eye of a REAL Korean mountain pass at late dusk. ONE device: the ground as a saddle. Two pine hills pinch a high pass; a small STONE RING fortress sits on the pinch — weathered stone, one hongye gate, a tiny giwa munru; west of the ring a wide high field; east a packed-earth road home; below the west lip a black pine-pond as one dark disc. Keep the attached fortress architecture. Tiny yellow and blue specks of men dissolving. DAY GROUND on WHITE: paper-white haze sky, one low sun shaft raking the saddle. No readable faces. No army catalog. No ships. No text. No watermark. PAINTED STILL — no people, no figures, no faces, no hands anywhere in the frame; the place or object IS the subject. Sensual and suggestive by shape and motion alone, never anatomical, never explicit. A 2:1 movie frame composed for a 2:1 letterbox crop (nothing important at the top or bottom edge). Hand-painted WATERCOLOR-AND-OIL: granulated wet-in-wet washes and broken-colour dabs for sky, water and stone, dry-brush texture, soft bleeding edges and a faint paper grain; oil glazes deepen the darks and a touch of impasto lands on the single brightest highlight. Romantic-painting layout: one bold shape, at least half the frame quiet negative space, distant detail dissolving into haze. Film tenebrism: one hard directional key (sun, moon or lamp) against big dark masses, a thin edge of real light along the subject, painted bokeh from small real lights. Beautiful, luminous, painterly. NOT photoreal, NOT 3D, NOT a cartoon. No text. No watermark. DAY GROUND: the frame is built on WHITE — a high-key, paper-white ground: pale bright sky, white haze and mist, sunlit plaster and pale stone dissolving into bare white paper at the edges, the shadows few, crisp and cool-grey; the figure is the dark, inked thing in a bright frame. Never a black void, never a dim dusk wash.
